entities.summary: Diogo de Silves is the presumed name of an obscure Portuguese explorer of the Atlantic who allegedly discovered the Azores islands in 1427. This event is significant because it marked the beginning of European exploration and colonization of the Atlantic islands. The Portuguese Empire, under the rule of King John I, had been expanding its territories in West Africa and the Atlantic islands since the 14th century. Diogo de Silves' voyage was part of this expansion, and it paved the way for further exploration and settlement of the Azores. The discovery of the Azores had significant consequences for the Portuguese Empire, as it provided a strategic location for trade and naval bases. The islands also became a major hub for the transatlantic slave trade, which had a profound impact on the demographics and culture of the Azores. The legacy of Diogo de Silves' voyage can be seen in the modern-day cultural and historical significance of the Azores, which remain a popular tourist destination and a symbol of Portuguese identity. The discovery of the Azores is also remembered as a significant moment in the history of exploration, marking the beginning of the Age of Exploration and the European colonization of the Americas.
